question:
What is the defined value of kB in the given equation?

kB = PV/TN
solution:
The correct answer is__** 1.38 × 10-23 J K-1.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **physical constant** known as **Boltzmann's constant** allows us to **calculate how much energy** is involved in the **random thermal movements** of the** constituent particles** of a substance.
 
• The **average kinetic energy of molecules** is** high **when the **temperature** of the gas molecules is** high,** according to **Austrian physicist Ludwig Boltzmann.**
 
• Temperature (R) ∝ Kinetic Energy (K.E.)
 
• The equation would be:
 
• **PV = N x Kb x T.**
 
• Here, P is the **Pressure** in Pascals, V is the **volume** in meter cubes, N = **No of molecules **of the gas, T = **Temperature**, and Kb is **Boltzmann’s constant.**
 
• S.I. unit of Kb =** Joule per kelvin.**
 
• The value of Boltzmann’s constant Kb in CGS is given by** 1.3806542×10−16 erg / Kelvin**.
 
• Dimensional formula of Boltzmann’s constant** :ML²T⁻²Θ⁻¹.**
 
• Boltzmann’s constant in electron Volt (eV) is equal to **0.000086173324 eV/ kelvin.**
